Listen to this article Share Arik Air, Nigerian domestic carrier, plans to expand its flight capacity in 2027, banking on stabilising aviation fuel prices and easing domestic inflation to revive passenger demand months after soaring Jet-A1 costs nearly grounded local operations. Advertisement Advertisement Speaking on Wednesday on the sidelines of the International Civil Aviation Organization’s (ICAO) global transport conference in Montreal, Ailemen Charles Arumemi-Johnson, Chief Commercial Officer of Arik Air, disclosed that the airline intends to reintroduce three aircraft back into active service as operating pressures gradually moderate. While acknowledging that aviation fuel remains costly, Arumemi-Johnson noted that the severe price spike triggered earlier in the year by the conflict in Iran has begun to retreat. Read also: Air Peace acquires another Embraer 190 AIRC, strengthens fleet expansion drive Coupled with ongoing federal government efforts to rein in inflation, he said improving household purchasing power should stimulate stronger air travel demand. “We’re going to add capacity because we have the market,” Arumemi-Johnson said during the interview. “Once oil prices go down, ticket fares become cheaper. We just hope the war in Iran ends as quickly as possible.” Advertisement Earlier in the year, acute jet fuel price surges forced airlines worldwide to trim flight schedules and hike ticket prices to protect margins. In Nigeria, the crisis escalated in April when domestic operators threatened a nationwide suspension of flight services starting April 20 unless urgent relief was provided on crippling Jet-A1 costs. Advertisement Read also: LAMATA responds to trending bus video, promises fleet expansion Domestic supply pressures have also been cushioned by the Dangote Refinery, which ramped up local jet fuel production to help bridge supply gaps sparked by the Middle East conflict. For Arik Air, bringing three additional aircraft back into service signals renewed confidence that moderating fuel expenses and macroeconomic stabilisation will support higher flight frequencies and more competitive airfares in 2027. Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha is the Aviation Correspondent at BusinessDay Media Limited, publishers of BusinessDay Newspapers. She is also the Deputy Editor, BusinessDay Weekender Magazine, the Saturday Weekend edition of BusinessDay. She holds a BSC in Mass Communication from the prestigious University of Nigeria, Nsukka and a Masters degree in Marketing at the University of Lagos. As the lead writer on the aviation desk, Ifeoma is responsible and in charge of the three weekly aviation and travel pages in BusinessDay and BDSunday. She also overseas and edits all pages of BusinessDay Saturday Weekender. She has written various investigative, features and news stories in aviation and business related issues and has been severally nominated for award in the category of Aviation Writer of the Year by the Nigeria Media Nite-Out awards; one of the Nigeria’s most prestigious media awards ceremonies. Ifeoma is a one-time winner of the prestigious Nigeria Media Merit Award under the 'Aviation Writer of the Year' Category. She is the 2025 Eloy Award winner under the Print Media Journalist category. She has undergone several journalism trainings by various prestigious organisations. Ifeoma is also a fellow of the Female Reporters Leadership Fellowship of the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism.
